name: Peter
prompt: Where did Peter minister, serve, and die?
summary: Peter's ministry expanded beyond the original Jerusalem community. He visited Cornelius in Caesarea, showing that the gospel was being opened to people from every nation, and he continued serving the growing church despite opposition. His first letter encourages believers to keep their hope, live holy lives, and remain faithful through suffering. The map follows the tradition that Peter eventually served and was martyred in Rome, although the biblical record does not give a complete account of his final years.

name: Paul
prompt: Where did Paul minister, serve, and die?
summary: Paul traveled through the eastern Mediterranean because he believed the gospel should reach the nations and new churches needed teaching and encouragement. He preached, trained leaders, strengthened believers, and continued his work through beatings, opposition, imprisonment, and legal trials. Acts ends with Paul in Rome, still welcoming visitors and proclaiming the kingdom of God. Italy is therefore the final location shown on the map; his martyrdom there is preserved by later Christian tradition rather than described in detail by Acts.

name: Mark
prompt: Where did Mark minister, serve, and die?
summary: Mark served the early Christian mission as John Mark and is connected with the apostolic community in the New Testament. His Gospel presents Jesus through His powerful works, suffering, death, and resurrection, giving the church a message meant to be carried to the world. Coptic Orthodox tradition remembers Mark as the person who brought the faith to Alexandria, Egypt, and established the Alexandrian church. He is also remembered as a martyr who suffered because he continued preaching Christ.

name: Thomas
prompt: Where did Thomas minister, serve, and die?
summary: Thomas was one of the Twelve and is remembered especially for moving from uncertainty to a direct confession of the risen Christ. That testimony became part of the apostles' mission to carry the gospel beyond Jerusalem and into distant cultures. The Bible does not give a detailed travel itinerary for Thomas after the resurrection, but longstanding church tradition says he traveled east, evangelized communities in India, and was killed because of his preaching. India is the traditional destination represented on the map.

name: Andrew
prompt: Where did Andrew minister, serve, and die?
summary: Andrew was among the first disciples called to follow Jesus, and he helped bring others to hear and follow Him. After the resurrection, his purpose was to bear witness and help extend the church beyond its first community in Jerusalem. Scripture does not preserve a complete account of Andrew's later travels. Church tradition places his preaching around the Black Sea and says he was martyred at Patras in Greece, where he continued serving despite opposition.

name: John
prompt: Where did John minister, serve, and die?
summary: John served as a close witness to Jesus' life, death, and resurrection, and his Gospel teaches about Christ's divine identity, love, truth, and faithful witness. He continued caring for the church and teaching believers to remain in fellowship with God even when false teaching and opposition threatened them. Later church tradition places John among the churches of Asia Minor, especially around Ephesus in present-day Turkey. Unlike several other apostles, John is traditionally remembered as dying naturally after a long life of ministry rather than by martyrdom.

name: James (son of Zebedee)
prompt: Where did James (son of Zebedee) die?
summary: James was one of the disciples especially close to Jesus and was called to share the apostolic witness. His ministry took place during the difficult early years of the church, when leaders faced pressure from both religious authorities and political rulers. Herod ordered James killed with the sword during a persecution of the church. This is one of the clearest apostolic death accounts in Acts and places his death in Jerusalem, in the land of Israel.

name: Philip
prompt: Where did Philip minister, serve, and die?
summary: Philip helped carry the message of Christ across cultural and geographic boundaries. The apostolic mission required servants who could explain the faith, welcome new believers, and continue despite resistance. Scripture gives limited information about Philip's later years, so the map follows the tradition that he served in Phrygia and Hierapolis, in modern Turkey. He is traditionally remembered as a martyr because he continued preaching in the face of opposition.

name: Bartholomew
prompt: Where did Bartholomew minister, serve, and die?
summary: Bartholomew was one of the Twelve chosen to accompany Christ and bear witness to Him. After the resurrection, his calling was to take that witness beyond the places where Jesus had taught and to serve people who had not yet heard the gospel. The biblical books do not preserve a detailed route for his later ministry. Ancient church tradition places his mission in Armenia and neighboring regions, where he is remembered as a martyr who suffered for continuing to preach.

name: Matthew
prompt: Where did Matthew minister, serve, and die?
summary: Matthew was a tax collector when Jesus called him, and his life shows that Christ sends unlikely people into faithful service. His Gospel presents Jesus as the promised Messiah and connects discipleship with teaching, obedience, mercy, and mission. The later destination of Matthew is not fixed by a detailed biblical itinerary. One longstanding tradition places his later mission and death in Ethiopia, where he is remembered as a witness who continued preaching despite opposition.

name: James (son of Alphaeus)
prompt: Where did James (son of Alphaeus) minister, serve, and die?
summary: James the son of Alphaeus was one of the Twelve apostles chosen by Jesus, but the New Testament preserves very little narrative detail about his later work. That silence reminds us that many servants helped build the church without having their journeys recorded in detail. Because later traditions differ about his destination and death, this map uses Jerusalem and the land of Israel as a cautious traditional location rather than presenting a disputed route as certain history.

name: Thaddeus (Jude)
prompt: Where did Thaddeus (Jude) minister, serve, and die?
summary: Jude taught believers to hold firmly to the faith, remember the apostles' teaching, resist ungodliness, and show mercy with wisdom. His message reflects the kind of work the apostles carried into communities facing confusion, false teaching, and pressure to compromise. Later church tradition associates Jude with missionary work in Armenia and surrounding lands, often alongside Simon the Zealot, and remembers him as a martyr. That later geography is traditional rather than fully narrated in Scripture.

name: Simon the Zealot
prompt: Where did Simon the Zealot minister, serve, and die?
summary: Simon the Zealot was one of the Twelve called by Jesus, showing that people with different backgrounds and convictions were gathered into one apostolic mission. The New Testament does not preserve a detailed account of Simon's later route. Ancient tradition places his mission eastward in the region of Persia, including territory in modern Iran, where he is remembered as a martyr who faced hostility because he would not stop proclaiming Christ.

name: Matthias
prompt: Where did Matthias minister, serve, and die?
summary: Matthias was chosen to take Judas' place because he had accompanied Jesus' ministry and could witness to the resurrection. His selection shows the early church seeking a faithful servant through prayer and discernment. The New Testament does not record a complete travel history for Matthias after his appointment. Later tradition places his preaching around the Black Sea, including areas associated with modern Georgia, where he is remembered as a missionary who faced opposition for the gospel.
